name: Filatex India Ltd
title: Filatex India Ltd-$ - 526227 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Filatex Q1 FY27 volumes flat QoQ at 89,872 MT with production cut to 84,075 MT in April; margins held on pass-through, Ecosis chemical recycling (1 to 75 TPD) targets ~INR80-85 crore EBITDA, with stabilisation risk and no prior-guidance check.

utilisation.quote: production during the quarter was 84,075 metric tons against 94,996 in Q1 FY26

capex.peers_comment: Management said international recycling peers' capex per ton is at least 3x to 5x more than Filatex's and nothing is coming before calendar 2027.
capex.quote: Our comprehensive capital expenditure program of approximately INR690 crores continues to progress steadily.

summary.headline: Filatex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.3% QoQ to INR1,145 crore and PAT to INR49.1 crore, driven by pass-through raw material prices.
summary.overview: Revenue rose 16.3% QoQ to INR1,145 crore on higher realisations, while volumes were flat QoQ at 89,872 MT. PBT rose to INR65.87 crore and PAT to INR49.1 crore, helped by inventory gains of about INR15-17 crore expected in the quarter. Production fell to 84,075 MT from 94,996 MT a year earlier as the company cut run-rates in April to avoid carrying high-cost inventory. Management focused on the Ecosis textile-to-textile chemical recycling project, which is still under installation with commercial operations guided for end-October/early-November 2026.

segments.name: Polyester (Filatex standalone)
segments.commentary: Volumes flat QoQ at 89,872 MT; April run-rates were cut due to high raw material costs, then sales recovered in May-June from carried inventory. Management said polyester yarn prices rose in line with raw materials, which were about 20% higher than pre-Iran-conflict levels, and margins were said to be intact or better.

segments.name: Ecosis (chemical recycling subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Greenfield plant at 75 TPD (pilot was 1 TPD) is under machine installation; commercial operations guided for end-October/early-November 2026, with possible 15-day to few-month slippage. Management guided EBITDA of INR80-85 crore at full run-rate, with about 80% utilisation in FY28 and near 100% by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Ecosis: stabilisation expected within 3-5 months of start-up, i.e. by end-FY27; utilisation guided above 80% for FY28 on average; FY27 utilisation not guaranteed, with better guidance promised by Dec/Jan.

Ecosis EBITDA guided at INR80-85 crore; management said FY27 contribution from Ecosis would be about INR40-50 crore... analysts' calculation of INR220-230 crore total EBITDA uplift implies about 40% accrues in FY27; Ecosis top-line contribution about INR150-200 crore this year and about INR400 crore in a full year.
Ecosis long-term EBITDA margin guided at minimum 30%, with plans for 2 more 1.5 lakh-ton plants in 2-3 years, one in India and one overseas.
Steam sale project: capex INR80-85 crore, EBITDA about INR60 crore, commercialisation by September 2026; 60% of capacity tied up, rest under discussion.
Peak net debt guided at INR150-200 crore at end-FY27 (including working capital, excluding LCs); gross debt INR350-370 crore by year-end; debt-to-equity comfort level 0.4.
Standalone FY27/FY28 revenue guidance of INR4,500 crore and INR4,800 crore was not reaffirmed; management said top line depends on raw material prices and it is more confident on bottom line.
Brownfield PFI expansion (FDY, POY, DTY): 50% by September 2026, balance 50% by October 2026. Total capex programme about INR690-700 crore; INR450-500 crore already deployed.
capex_capacity: Total capex programme approximately INR690 crore (analyst referenced INR700 crore), with INR450-500 crore deployed to date.
Brownfield PFI expansion adds FDY, POY and DTY capacity; 55,000 MT POY-related capacity, of which 14,000-15,000 MT is DTY.

Ecosis: 75 TPD textile-to-textile chemical recycling plant; machines under installation; commercial start end-October/early-November 2026; capex per ton stated at 3x to 5x lower than international peers.

Steam distribution project: capex INR80-85 crore via turbine change and piping, selling surplus captive-plant steam to neighbouring industries at about INR3/kg versus INR6-7/kg for gas-based steam; commercialisation expected September 2026.
Automation at Dahej facility; approximately 180-200 staff reduction planned, with INR4-5 crore annual savings.
Renewable energy programme progressing to increase green power share.
demand_pricing: Customers adopted need-based buying with shorter booking cycles and lean inventories; April was weak with crude at $110-115 and labour shortages, while May-June improved and July was similar to June.

Import duty on PTA and MEG was reduced for about 3 months and lapsed on 30 June; current duty is 5% plus 10% surcharge (5.5%). Management said the EBITDA impact was minimal as the duty was a pass-through.
Ecosis: 15-20% of planned production under commitments from two parties (Decathlon via Indica Sporting Goods MoU and American & Efird Global), with NDA-bound discussions with other brands.
Ecosis pricing: recycled yarn sells at about $2.0-2.3/kg (about INR180-190); chips sold in small quantities at about INR140-150/kg. Management said Chinese peers price 10-15% above Filatex's pricing.
Management cited a 3-5 million tonne demand pool for recycled polyester versus about 1 lakh tonne of operating global capacity.
Competitors' recycling plants are expected from calendar 2027 onwards, mostly in 2028-29.
Product mix: more FDY and cationic yarn; specialised products earn INR3-5/kg more than general products.
